title: Euclid Toolkit
statement:
Use Euclid’s algorithm for GCD and LCM and extended Euclid to compute modular inverses.

Input
q, then q lines OP a b. GCD and LCM use two nonnegative integers. Define gcd(0,0)=0 and lcm(a,0)=lcm(0,b)=0. For INV, a may be signed and b≥2 is the modulus.

Output
Print each result. For INV print the smallest nonnegative inverse, or NONE if no inverse exists.

Constraints
1 ≤ q ≤ 200000. Inputs have absolute value at most 10⁹.

samples.input:
6
GCD 0 0
GCD 54 24
LCM 6 8
LCM 7 0
INV -3 11
INV 4 10
